verdict.summary: No security vulnerabilities introduced. The PR adjusts timeout constants, model lineup, and adds a static budget invariant plus synth timeout handling — all configuration/error-handling changes with no impact on auth, secrets, injection, or supply-chain risk.
verdict.confidenceReason: The diff touches only timeout constants, model name strings, and error-handling logic; no security-sensitive code paths (auth, secrets, injection, permissions) are modified.

verdict.summary: The PR is well-structured for performance: it fixes zombie model calls via composed-signal passing, caps pre-flight retrieval, and reduces wasted retry latency. Two concerns remain: the pre-flight retrieval call doesn't receive the composed signal (same zombie-call pattern fixed for specialists/synth but missed here), and both logic and performance fallbacks now concentrate on Moonshot (kimi-k2.5), reducing fallback diversity under provider outages.
verdict.confidenceReason: The diff shows the critical signal-passing fix clearly, and the fallback concentration is verifiable from the config changes; the pre-flight signal gap requires inferring that cachedRetrieve wraps an HTTP call, which the catch-block comment confirms.

findings.headline: Pre-flight retrieval doesn't receive composed signal — zombie Vectorize call on timeout
findings.body: The specialist and synth `withComposedTimeout` calls were correctly upgraded from `() => runSpecialist({signal: orchCtrl.signal})` to `(signal) => runSpecialist({signal})` so the composed signal cancels the in-flight model call at the per-role timeout. But the pre-flight call at line ~349 still uses `() => preflightCache.cachedRetrieve({...})` — no signal is passed through. If the 15s pre-flight timeout fires, `withComposedTimeout` rejects the await but the underlying Vectorize HTTP request inside `retrieveChunks` keeps running until the 400s orchestrator wall fires. The catch-block comment even acknowledges this: 'the cache itself wraps the fetcher in its own try/catch so its log will eventually capture the fetcher's outcome once the background call settles.' A slow Vectorize round-trip thus holds a network connection and server-side resources for up to 385s after we've given up. Fix: change to `(signal) => preflightCache.cachedRetrieve({...fetcher: () => retrieveChunks({..., signal}), ...})` (if `retrieveChunks` accepts a signal), or at minimum pass the composed signal to the `retrieveChunks` fetcher so the HTTP call is aborted at 15s.

findings.headline: Moonshot fallback concentration — logic + performance both fall back to kimi-k2.5:cloud
findings.body: After this PR, both `SPECIALIST_CONFIGS.logic.fallback` and `SPECIALIST_CONFIGS.performance.fallback` route to `kimi-k2.5:cloud` (Moonshot). Previously, performance fell back to `glm-5.1:cloud` (Z.ai) — a different provider. Under a Moonshot regional outage, two specialists lose their fallback simultaneously. If both primaries are also experiencing issues (e.g., DeepSeek capacity pressure on logic, glm-5.1 transient 503 on performance), quorum could drop below 2/4, causing the ensemble to fail. The v2 risk register notes this but accepts it. Mitigation: consider rotating one fallback to a third provider (e.g., `qwen3-coder-next:cloud` for performance) to restore two-provider fallback coverage, or add a runtime check that warns when >1 specialist shares the same fallback provider.

verdict.summary: The PR adds critical timeout handling and model lineup changes but ships without runtime tests for the two new error-handling paths (synth timeout, pre-flight timeout) and the composed signal cancellation. The static configuration tests are present, but the runtime behavior that the PR explicitly depends on is untested, creating regression risk for the production fix.
verdict.confidenceReason: The PR body itself lists required runtime tests that are absent from the diff; the missing coverage is unambiguous and directly impacts the reliability of the ensemble fix.

findings.headline: Synth timeout handling (try/catch at line 432) has no runtime test
findings.body: The new try/catch around `withComposedTimeout(runSynthesizer, ...)` distinguishes synth-local timeout from outer-orch abort and writes `synthesizer.timedOut: true` + `fellBackReason: 'synth_timeout'`. The PR body (test #1) explicitly requires a test that mocks `runSynthesizer` to timeout and verifies the telemetry shape, but no such test exists in the diff. Without this test, a future refactor could silently revert to the old `internalError: 'Operation aborted'` behavior. Add a test that mocks `runSynthesizer` to reject with an AbortError on the synth's own signal (not the outer signal) and asserts `telemetry.synthesizer.timedOut === true` and `telemetry.fellBackReason === 'synth_timeout'`.

findings.headline: Pre-flight retrieval timeout (try/catch at line 335) has no runtime test
findings.body: The new try/catch around `withComposedTimeout(cachedRetrieve, RETRIEVAL_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS, ...)` sets `preflightChunks = null` on timeout and continues with empty snapshot. The PR body (test #4) requires a test that mocks `retrieveChunks` to take >15s and verifies the orchestrator proceeds with empty snapshot and sets `retrievalCacheStats.preflightTimedOut: true`. No such test exists. Add a test that mocks `retrieveChunks` to hang or reject after 15s and asserts the orchestrator does not throw and `retrievalSnapshot` is empty.

findings.headline: Composed signal propagation in runSpecialist and runSynthesizer is untested
findings.body: The PR changes `runSpecialist` and `runSynthesizer` to receive a composed signal from `withComposedTimeout` instead of `orchCtrl.signal` directly. This ensures the underlying model call is cancelled on specialist/synth timeout, not just the await wrapper. There is no test that verifies the signal is correctly wired: e.g., mock `attemptChat` to check that it receives an abort signal that fires when the specialist timeout elapses. Without this test, a future change could accidentally pass the wrong signal and leave model calls running until the outer 400s wall. Add a test that mocks `attemptChat` and asserts it is called with a signal that aborts after `SPECIALIST_TIMEOUT_MS`.

findings.headline: Performance fallback model (kimi-k2.5) usage is not tested at runtime
findings.body: The PR promotes `glm-5.1:cloud` to primary and sets `kimi-k2.5:cloud` as fallback for the performance specialist. The PR body (test #5) requires a test that mocks the primary to fail and asserts `runSpecialist({role:'performance'})` returns a verdict with `modelUsed === 'kimi-k2.5:cloud'`. No such test exists. Add a test that mocks `attemptChat` to reject on the primary and succeed on the fallback, then asserts the verdict is non-null and `modelUsed` is the fallback model.

findings.headline: PR body claims MAX_CALLS_PER_ENSEMBLE_RUN is 16 but test asserts 15
findings.body: The PR body says 'max-calls-per-PR derivation (16, was 17)' but the test at line 502 asserts `MAX_CALLS_PER_ENSEMBLE_RUN` is 15. The test is correct (logic retries dropped to 1 gives 3+3+3+3+3=15). The PR body has a documentation error. Update the PR body to say 15, was 16 (pre-Phase-4a.1 with logic retries=2 gave 4+3+3+3+3=16).

log.query:
fix(phase4a.1): timeouts + perf primary + synth timeout handling

**Fixes Phase 4 ensemble production failure** (1/15 fully-healthy verdicts in shadow).

## Root causes (from shadow telemetry analysis at `.claude/research/phase4b-shadow/`)

1. `deepseek-v4-pro:cloud` (logic) hits 90s wall on retries — 12/15 logic runs aborted
2. `kimi-k2.6:cloud` (synth) squeezed when specialist verdicts run long — 4/15 hit 240s outer timeout at 199-211s
3. `minimax-m2.1:cloud` (perf primary) unreliable — 6/12 successful runs came from `glm-5.1` fallback

## Patch

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| SPECIALIST_TIMEOUT_MS | 90s | 180s |
| SYNTHESIZER_TIMEOUT_MS | 120s | 180s |
| ORCHESTRATOR_TIMEOUT_MS | 240s | 400s |
| RESERVED_HEADROOM_MS | — | 40s |
| RETRIEVAL_PREFLIGHT_TIMEOUT_MS | — | 15s |
| logic.retries | 2 | 1 |
| performance.primary | minimax-m2.1:cloud | glm-5.1:cloud |
| performance.fallback | glm-5.1:cloud | kimi-k2.5:cloud |

Plus structural changes:
- Static budget invariant enforced at module load (`specialist + synth + headroom ≤ orch`)
- Pre-flight retrieval wrapped in `withComposedTimeout(15s)`; failure → empty snapshot per v3.1 §8
- Synth call wrapped in try/catch that distinguishes synth-local timeout from outer-orch abort. Synth-local timeout writes `synthesizer.timedOut: true` + `fellBackReason: 'synth_timeout'` (was bubbling as `internalError: 'Operation aborted'`)

## Tests

481 → 489. New: timeout invariant, exact values, pre-flight slack, per-role lineup, max-calls-per-PR derivation (16, was 17).

## Sign-off

- Codex: 'ship with 3 changes' (synth timeout handling, math, tests) — integrated
- Kimi K2.6: 'ship with 1 tweak' (orch ≥ 390s) — integrated as 400s

Specs: `.claude/handoff/arc-phase4a.1-patch-v2-LOCKED.md` (also v1 + shadow report).

## Test plan

- [ ] `npm test` 489/489 pass locally
- [ ] After deploy, monitor next 10 shadow records: corpus health flips from 1/15 → ≥7/10
- [ ] No regression on existing Phase 3 single-agent path (untouched)
